Minimal CATE demo data (oracle nuisances + pseudo-outcome)

Source: R/demo-data-cate.R
cate_demo_data.Rd

Generates a small synthetic dataset for experimenting with the CATE score. It returns \(X\), \(D\), \(Y\), along with oracle nuisance quantities: $$ m(x) \;=\; \mathbb{E}[Y \mid X=x] \;=\; m_{0}(x) \;+\; e(x)\,\tau(x) \, , \qquad e(x) \;=\; \Pr(D=1 \mid X=x) \, , $$ where \(m_{0}(x) = \mathbb{E}[Y \mid X=x, D=0]\) and \(\tau(x)\) is the treatment effect. It also returns the oracle AIPW pseudo-outcome.

Usage

cate_demo_data(
  n = 200,
  p = 2,
  design = c("simple", "hetero", "bump"),
  sigma = 0.5,
  clip = 0.001,
  seed = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  inject = NULL,
  inject_col = "aipw_oracle",
  idx_inject = 3L
)

Arguments

n

Integer sample size.

p

Integer feature dimension, at least 2.

design

Character; one of "simple", "hetero", "bump" for \(\tau(x)\).

sigma

Noise standard deviation in \(Y\).

clip

Propensity clipping in \((0,\,0.5)\); applied to \(e(x)\).

seed

Optional integer seed, used locally without changing the caller's RNG state. NULL uses the current stream.

x0

Optional numeric length-\(p\) target point (defaults to the zero vector).

inject

Optional, one of NULL, "na", "inf"; if provided, inject a single non-finite value into one of the returned columns (see inject_col) at row idx_inject; useful for testing runtime guards.

inject_col

Character; which column to corrupt when inject is not NULL. One of "Y", "aipw_oracle", "e_oracle", "m_oracle", "m0_oracle", "tau_oracle". Default "aipw_oracle".

idx_inject

Integer index to corrupt (default 3).

Value

A list with:

  • data: a data.frame with columns X1..Xp, D, Y, and oracle nuisances e_oracle (=\(e(X)\)), m_oracle (=\(m(X)\)), m0_oracle (=\(m_{0}(X)\)), m1_oracle (treated outcome mean), tau_oracle (=\(\tau(X)\)), aipw_oracle (oracle AIPW signal).

  • x0: the target point used (length \(p\)).

  • truth: list of closures tau_fn(x), e_fn(x), m0_fn(x), m_fn(x) to evaluate ground truth at any \(x\).

  • tau_x0: the true \(\tau(x_{0})\).

Details

No model fitting is performed; all quantities come from the DGP.

Examples

demo <- cate_demo_data(n = 200, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 1)
str(demo$data)
#> 'data.frame':	200 obs. of  10 variables:
#>  $ X1         : num  -0.626 0.184 -0.836 1.595 0.33 ...
#>  $ X2         : num  0.409 1.689 1.587 -0.331 -2.285 ...
#>  $ D          : int  1 0 1 0 1 0 0 0 1 0 ...
#>  $ Y          : num  0.21 -0.654 -1.885 2.932 4.772 ...
#>  $ e_oracle   : num  0.373 0.32 0.23 0.724 0.787 ...
#>  $ m_oracle   : num  0.0414 -0.3159 -1.3926 3.6498 4.1356 ...
#>  $ m0_oracle  : num  -0.0359 -0.5052 -1.4222 2.9262 3.6147 ...
#>  $ m1_oracle  : num  0.171 0.0861 -1.2931 3.926 4.2765 ...
#>  $ tau_oracle : num  0.207 0.591 0.129 1 0.662 ...
#>  $ aipw_oracle: num  0.31 0.81 -2.449 0.979 1.292 ...
demo$tau_x0
#> [1] 0.5
